Add a step

Source: R/pipeflow.R
pip_add.Rd

Adds a named step to the pipeline. Each step is a function whose parameters either hold constant defaults or reference the output of a prior step using formula notation (~step_name). Dependencies are validated when the step is added.

Usage

pip_add(
  x,
  step,
  fun,
  tags = character(0),
  after = length(x),
  params = list(),
  exec = "auto"
)

Arguments

x

A pipeflow pipeline object.

step

Unique step name.

fun

Function to execute for the step. Each function parameter needs a value: a default value in fun or an entry in params. Default values that are simple constants are resolved immediately. Default values that are formulas like ~other_step are treated as dependencies to those steps and resolved to the respective output values at runtime once the step is executed. A reference wrapped in try(), like ~try(other_step), accepts a failed input when the pipeline is run with on_error = "continue": instead of the output of the referenced step, the argument then receives a condition of class pipeflow_failure (see section 'Continuing after errors' in pip_run()). The function can refer to the running pipeline as .self (see section 'The pipeline as .self' in pip_add()).

tags

Optional character vector of tags belonging to the step. Can also be adjusted later using [pip_tag()].

after

Optional position after which the new step should be inserted (defaults to last position). Can be a step name or an integer index. If set to 0, the new step will be inserted at the beginning of the pipeline.

params

Optional named list of parameter values. They override the defaults of fun and give a value to parameters of fun that have no default. As in the defaults of fun, a formula like ~other_step refers to the output of another step. Names that are no parameters of fun add params to the step, which are passed on to fun as well, so fun needs a ... argument for them. Use cases for params are:

  1. Set param values programmatically, e.g. when adding steps in a loop or at runtime.

  2. Use existing functions whose parameters have no defaults, e.g. pip_add(p, "avg", mean, params = list(x = ~data, na.rm = TRUE)).

  3. Provide extra param values to "mark" dependencies that are defined in pipelines nested in a step, which ensures that it is re-executed when one of the nested param values change. See the nested pipelines vignette.

exec

Execution mode for this step. One of "auto", "split", "reduce" or "plain". Using execution mode exec = split, the output of the step is marked as partitioned output. In this mode, any step that depends on the split step (directly or indirectly) will have its output automatically mapped partition-wise during step execution. The reduce mode expects partitioned input and passes it through without mapping, while plain mode only accepts non-partitioned input and always intends to execute a single call. In a run with on_error = "continue", a mapped step that fails for some partition keys keeps the outputs of the other keys (see section 'Continuing after errors' in pip_run()). If a split step fails, a reduce step also accepts the resulting failure object when it takes it via ~try(). In summary:

  • auto: map if partitioned input appears, otherwise single call. Several partitioned inputs must have the same keys in the same order.

  • split: single call, then mark output as partitioned

  • reduce: single call, but only valid with partitioned input or, via ~try(), a failure object

  • plain: single call, only valid with non-partitioned input

Value

The updated pipeline, invisibly.

Details

If after was specified, the new step will be inserted after the given step or position. Be aware that in contrast to adding a step at the end, inserting a step in the middle is a rather expensive operation as it requires re-wiring parts of the internal pipeline structure, especially if the new step is inserted at an early position.

The pipeline as .self

A step function can refer to the pipeline that is being run as .self without declaring it as an argument, for example to set parameters or add steps at runtime, or to call .self$restart() or .self$halt() (see pip_run()). .self is always the full pipeline, also when a view is run. pipeflow provides it each time the step runs, but only if the body of the step function contains the name .self (also within functions defined in the body). Indirect access, such as get(".self"), is not detected.

A step that changes its own function, params or exec mode via .self, ends the run as "outdated". The same is true for other steps changed via .self. Lastly, .self is only valid while the step runs and released once the step was returned. For this reason, a step that returns a function referring to .self fails with object '.self' not found when called later.

Examples

# --- Tags, and view filtering ---
p <- pip_new("analysis") |>
  pip_add("load", \(n = 5) seq_len(n), tags = c("io", "raw")) |>
  pip_add("clean", \(x = ~load) x * 2, tags = c("io", "process")) |>
  pip_add("fit", \(x = ~clean) sum(x), tags = c("model", "core", "daily")) |>
  pip_add("report", \(x = ~fit) paste("result:", x), tags = "report")

pip_run(p)
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.612 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'analysis'
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.612 UTC]: Step 1/4 load
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.613 UTC]: Step 2/4 clean
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.614 UTC]: Step 3/4 fit
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.615 UTC]: Step 4/4 report
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.615 UTC]: Finished in 0.003 s (4 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
p
#> <pipeflow> analysis (4 steps)
#> -----------------------------
#>      step params depends state            out             tags
#> 1:   load      n          done      1,2,3,4,5           io,raw
#> 2:  clean      x    load  done  2, 4, 6, 8,10       io,process
#> 3:    fit      x   clean  done             30 model,core,daily
#> 4: report      x     fit  done     result: 30           report
#> -----------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-25 19:30:01 (0.003 s)
#> steps: 4 done

# Filter by tag using pip_view — keeps steps with any matching tag
pip_view(p, tags = "daily")
#> <pipeflow_view> analysis (1 of 4 steps)
#> ---------------------------------------
#>    step params depends state out             tags
#> 1:  fit      x   clean  done  30 model,core,daily
#> ---------------------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-25 19:30:01 (0.003 s)
#> steps: 1 done
pip_view(p, tags = "core")
#> <pipeflow_view> analysis (1 of 4 steps)
#> ---------------------------------------
#>    step params depends state out             tags
#> 1:  fit      x   clean  done  30 model,core,daily
#> ---------------------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-25 19:30:01 (0.003 s)
#> steps: 1 done
pip_view(p, tags = c("raw", "report"))
#> <pipeflow_view> analysis (2 of 4 steps)
#> ---------------------------------------
#>      step params depends state        out   tags
#> 1:   load      n          done  1,2,3,4,5 io,raw
#> 2: report      x     fit  done result: 30 report

#> steps: 2 done

# --- Split / reduce execution modes ---
q <- pip_new("split-demo") |>
  pip_add("data", \(x = iris) x) |>
  pip_add("split", \(x = ~data) split(x, x$Species),
    exec = "split"
  ) |>
  pip_add("stats", \(x = ~split) summary(x)) |>
  pip_add("combine", \(x = ~stats) do.call(rbind, x),
    exec = "reduce"
  )

pip_run(q)

# --- Insert a step at a specific position with 'after' ---
p2 <- pip_new("insert-demo") |>
  pip_add("load", \(x = 1) x) |>
  pip_add("fit", \(x = ~load) x + 1)
p2
#> <pipeflow> insert-demo (2 steps)
#> --------------------------------
#>    step params depends state
#> 1: load      x           new
#> 2:  fit      x    load   new
#> --------------------------------
#> <ready> last run: never
#> steps: 2 new
pip_add(p2, "clean", \(x = ~load) x * 2, after = "load")
p2  # "load", "clean", "fit" — inserted after "load"
#> <pipeflow> insert-demo (3 steps)
#> --------------------------------
#>     step params depends state
#> 1:  load      x           new
#> 2: clean      x    load   new
#> 3:   fit      x    load   new
#> --------------------------------
#> <ready> last run: never
#> steps: 3 new

# after = 0 inserts the new step at the very beginning
pip_add(p2, "preload", \(x = 1) x, after = 0)
p2
#> <pipeflow> insert-demo (4 steps)
#> --------------------------------
#>       step params depends state
#> 1: preload      x           new
#> 2:    load      x           new
#> 3:   clean      x    load   new
#> 4:     fit      x    load   new
#> --------------------------------
#> <ready> last run: never
#> steps: 4 new

# --- Provide parameter values with 'params' ---
# 'params' override the defaults of the function ...
p3 <- pip_new("params-demo") |>
  pip_add("data", \(x = c(1, NA, 3)) x) |>
  pip_add("scale", \(x = ~data, factor = 1) x * factor,
    params = list(factor = 10)
  ) |>
  # ... and give values to parameters without default, e.g. of mean()
  pip_add("avg", mean, params = list(x = ~scale, na.rm = TRUE))
pip_run(p3)
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.642 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'params-demo'
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.642 UTC]: Step 1/3 data
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.643 UTC]: Step 2/3 scale
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.643 UTC]: Step 3/3 avg
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.644 UTC]: Finished in 0.002 s (3 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
p3
#> <pipeflow> params-demo (3 steps)
#> --------------------------------
#>     step   params depends state      out
#> 1:  data        x          done  1,NA, 3
#> 2: scale x,factor    data  done 10,NA,30
#> 3:   avg  x,na.rm   scale  done       20
#> --------------------------------
#> <ready> last run: 2026-10-25 19:30:01 (0.002 s)
#> steps: 3 done
p3[["avg", "out"]] # 20
#> [1] 20

# Extra params are passed via `...`
p4 <- pip_new("dots-demo") |>
  pip_add("load", \(x = 1, ...) c(x, ...), params = list(size = 42))
pip_run(p4)
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.647 UTC]: Starting run of pipeflow 'dots-demo'
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.647 UTC]: Step 1/1 load
#> info [2026-10-25 19:30:01.648 UTC]: Finished in 0.001 s (1 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed)
p4[["load", "out"]] # c(1, size = 42)
#>      size 
#>    1   42
